subsection: 1. Classification, nutritional significance and contribution to the diet

notes.b: Fish and shellfish fall into three groups. The groups are based mainly on where the fat is found, and shellfish are then split by the kind of shell they have.
points: White fish have little or no fat in the flesh, because their fat is stored in the liver (this is why cod liver oil exists). Examples are cod, haddock, whiting, plaice and sole.
Oily fish have fat spread through the flesh. Examples are salmon, trout, mackerel, herring and fresh tuna.
Crustacean shellfish have a hard, jointed outer shell. Examples are lobster, crab and prawns.
Mollusc shellfish have a soft body inside a hard shell with hinged halves that open and close. Examples are oysters, mussels and cockles.

Fish flesh is made of short muscle fibres called myomeres, separated by thin layers of connective tissue (the tough tissue that holds muscle together). With less connective tissue than meat, fish is tender, cooks quickly and is easy to digest.
The flesh of fish is about 65 to 80 per cent water, 0 to 18 per cent fat and 16 to 18 per cent HBV (high biological value) protein.
Water and fat are inversely related: the fattier the fish, the less water its flesh contains.
notes.tip: When asked to classify fish, name white, oily and shellfish, split shellfish into crustaceans and molluscs, and give an example of each. Don't call white fish fat-free, and use fresh tuna as your oily example. Remember oysters, mussels and cockles are molluscs, while prawns, crab and lobster are crustaceans.

notes.b: Fish is valued mainly for its protein, its fat (which differs between white and oily fish) and a wide range of vitamins and minerals. Each nutrient below comes with the fish that supplies it.
points: Protein: fish is a source of high biological value (HBV) protein, which supplies all the essential amino acids (the ones the body cannot make) needed for growth and repair.
Fat: white fish has almost no fat in the flesh, while oily fish is high in polyunsaturated fat, including the omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA. Fat-soluble vitamins are carried in this oil.
Carbohydrate: fish contains none, so it is best served with a starchy food.
B group vitamins are supplied by all fish.
Vitamins A and D are supplied by oily fish and by fish liver oils such as cod liver oil. Vitamin C is supplied by oysters, but fish is otherwise a poor source of it.
Iodine and fluorine come from sea fish, and phosphorus, potassium and zinc from most fish.
Calcium comes from canned fish eaten with the soft, edible bones, such as sardines and canned salmon, and from shellfish. Iron comes from shellfish and sardines.
Cholesterol is present in shellfish, which matters for anyone on a low-cholesterol diet. Water makes up 65 to 80 per cent of the flesh.
notes.tip: A nutritive value answer needs four to six points, each with its food source, such as 'iodine from sea fish'. Fish is not a source of vitamin C in general (oysters only), of carbohydrate, or of much iron.

notes.h: Omega-3 fatty acids and vitamin D in oily fish
notes.b: Oily fish is the main food source of these two nutrients, and both do important jobs in the body.
points: Essential fatty acids are polyunsaturated fatty acids that the body cannot make in the amounts it needs, so they must be obtained from food.
Omega-3 fatty acids are polyunsaturated, not saturated, and oily fish is their main dietary source. The types found in it are EPA and DHA.
Omega-3 fatty acids make blood platelets (the cell fragments that help blood clot) less sticky, so fewer blood clots form.
Omega-3 fatty acids reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and circulatory disease, because fewer clots and less cholesterol mean the blood vessels are less likely to block.
Omega-3 fatty acids reduce the build-up of cholesterol in the arteries and can help lower high blood pressure.
DHA also forms part of brain and eye tissue.
Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin found in oily fish and fish liver oils. It helps the body absorb calcium (and phosphorus), giving healthy bones and teeth.

A lack of vitamin D causes rickets in children and osteomalacia (soft bones) in adults. Vitamin D (the form is D3, cholecalciferol) is heat-stable: it is not destroyed by normal cooking and is not affected by oxygen, acids or alkalis.
notes.tip: If asked for the benefits of omega-3, give clots, heart attack, stroke and circulation, cholesterol and blood pressure. Vitamin D questions ask for its type, properties, functions and deficiency, so cover fat-soluble, heat-stable, calcium absorption and rickets.

notes.h: Dietetic value and contribution to the diet
notes.b: Dietetic value means how well fish suits the needs of different people and diets. A good answer links each feature of fish to a person or diet that benefits from it.
points: Fish is easy to digest, because its short muscle fibres and low connective tissue make the flesh soft. This suits children, the elderly, convalescents and invalids.
Its HBV protein supports growth in children and adolescents and repair of tissue in all age groups, and fish is a good alternative to meat in the main meal.
White fish is low in fat and energy, so it suits low-calorie, low-fat and weight-reducing diets.

Oily fish is recommended for people at risk of coronary heart disease, or with high cholesterol or high blood pressure. Its polyunsaturated fats, including omega-3, are linked to lower blood cholesterol and a lower risk of heart disease.
Shellfish contains cholesterol, so people on a low-cholesterol diet should take it with care.
Fish contains no carbohydrate, so it should be served with starchy foods such as potatoes, rice, pasta or bread. Fish in breadcrumbs, batter or sauce does contain some carbohydrate.
Iodine in sea fish helps prevent goitre (a swelling of the thyroid gland in the neck caused by too little iodine).
Fish is versatile: it can be prepared by many cooking methods and cooks quickly, which saves time and fuel. Canned and frozen fish products make fish available all year, out of season.

The Irish healthy eating guidelines (the Department of Health Food Pyramid, with FSAI guidance) place fish on the shelf with meat, poultry, eggs, beans and nuts, and advise eating fish regularly, including oily fish.
notes.tip: Examiners ask for five or six points on the contribution to the diet, so pick the ones above that match the groups named. When evaluating fish, also state its limitations: it lacks carbohydrate, and has little iron (except shellfish and sardines) and little vitamin C.

notes.b: Fish is not a complete food, and some people must avoid it. Eating habits for different fish have also changed over the years for clear reasons.
points: Fish lacks carbohydrate, and has little iron (except shellfish and sardines) and little vitamin C, so it cannot be the only food in a meal.
Fish, crustaceans and molluscs are each among the allergens that must be highlighted on food labels under Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, because they can cause serious reactions in some people.
Salmon and trout consumption rose because of greater awareness of the health benefits of oily fish and the growth of fish farming.
White fish was affected by over-fishing, depleted stocks and fishing laws, although it is still part of a healthy diet.
Shellfish and tuna consumption rose because of foreign travel and eating abroad, trendy recipes, falling cost and farming.
notes.tip: For reasons for trends in fish consumption, give health awareness, farming, over-fishing and stock depletion, travel and cost, matched to the type of fish.

keyTerms.definition: A short muscle segment; the flesh of fish is made of these short fibres, separated by thin layers of connective tissue.
Lean fish with almost no fat in the flesh, such as cod, haddock and plaice.
Fish with high fat content in the flesh, rich in polyunsaturated fat, omega-3 fatty acids and vitamins A and D.
Crustaceans and molluscs, such as prawns, lobster, mussels and oysters, eaten as seafood.
Protein that contains all the essential amino acids in the proportions the body needs.
Polyunsaturated fatty acids, found mainly in oily fish, that the body cannot make and must obtain from food.
Fatty acids that the body cannot make, so they must be supplied in the diet.
A vitamin that dissolves in fat rather than water, such as vitamin D in oily fish.

factCards.term: Four benefits of omega-3 fatty acids
factCards.definition: They reduce the risk of heart attack, reduce the risk of stroke, reduce blood clotting and reduce the build-up of cholesterol.

factCards.term: Two minerals supplied by sea fish

questions.prompt: Compare oily fish with white fish in terms of fat content, and name two nutrients that oily fish supplies in greater amounts than white fish.
questions.model: Oily fish has high fat in its flesh, mostly polyunsaturated, while white fish has almost no fat in the flesh. Oily fish supplies omega-3 fatty acids (EPA and DHA). Oily fish also supplies vitamins A and D. Any two of these nutrients earn the marks.

questions.prompt: Discuss the nutritive value of fish and its dietetic value in the diet, referring to white fish, oily fish and shellfish.
questions.model: Nutritive value: fish is a source of HBV protein containing all essential amino acids. White fish has almost no fat, while oily fish supplies polyunsaturated fat with omega-3 fatty acids and vitamins A and D. All fish supplies B group vitamins. Sea fish supplies iodine and fluorine; most fish supplies phosphorus, potassium and zinc. Canned fish with soft bones supplies calcium; shellfish and sardines supply iron; oysters supply vitamin C. Fish contains no carbohydrate. Shellfish contains cholesterol. Dietetic value: fish is easy to digest and suits children, the elderly and convalescents. Its protein supports growth and repair. It can replace meat. White fish suits low-fat and low-calorie diets. Omega-3 fats reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and circulatory disease, so oily fish suits people with heart disease. Fish should be served with starchy foods because it contains no carbohydrate. It cooks quickly and can be prepared many ways. Irish healthy eating guidelines from the Department of Health recommend regular fish, including oily fish.
